source.title: Central-Volksblatt
source.locator: Front page, lower right column, Die Armee Mackensen.

visual_checks.finding: The original gives no. 265, Arnsberg and Werl, Thursday 14 November 1918, and 63rd year.
The original agency label is WTB; the dateline is Berlin, 12 November. The report attributes its information to the German liaison officer in Budapest.

visual_checks.short_source_phrase: der 11. Armee und der Armee Mackensen je 6 Züge täglich
visual_checks.finding: The six daily trains are stated for each of the two named armies.

summary: The newspaper reports that the Hungarian government had made six trains per day available to each of the Eleventh Army and Mackensen army for evacuation.
historical_connection: Independent contemporary press context for the provisioning and passage problems discussed in an-army-trying-to-get-home.md.
limits: The report is a public agency dispatch, not an inspected train schedule or execution log.
The dispatch date, 12 November, differs from the newspaper date, 14 November, and precedes the Belgrade convention of 13 November.
No exact correspondence chain with the Arad supply request is established.
No ciphertext coordinate, plaintext letter, train capacity or completed journey is inferred.
